claim: On data_seed 1 (N=64, e<=0.5, 4 layers, d_model=64), training to 1500 steps makes force beat its best-of-5 control persistently in all 3 seeds. Read from the trajectories, force first holds >= 0.1 at step 400 (seed 75), 450 (seed 77) and 600 (seed 76), and ends at margins 0.196, 0.193 and 0.167 (R2 0.738/0.718/0.684 vs controls 0.542/0.525/0.517). accel_step stays roughly flat: it gains 0.006-0.018 after step 600 and ends at 0.156/0.160/0.177 (R2 0.92-0.93 vs controls 0.75-0.77). Headroom-normalised, accel_step still leads force in every seed (0.66-0.71 vs 0.35-0.43).
confidence_note: All three predictions held: force formed persistently by step 1500 in 3 of 3 seeds, final force margin was >= 0.11 in each, and accel_step moved less than 0.03 from its step-600 value. All runs completed 1500 of 1500 steps, the force control_spread (0.030-0.061) is below the 0.1 bar, and the controls differ by under 0.03 across seeds, so the margins are not control noise. Three caveats limit what this means. (1) In these 1500-step runs, force margin at step 600 is already 0.104-0.138, but the 600-step runs with the same seeds and data were at 0.085-0.099. The original 'no force code' null was therefore partly an artefact of where training stopped or of the lr schedule horizon, not only of total step count. (2) Force only crosses the bar after its best layer moves from 4 to 1 (the distance layer, distance margin 0.47-0.66) at steps 250-400. Layer-4 force never exceeds about 0.085. So this force signal may be a nonlinear read of distance and orbit scale rather than an m2-weighted force. Regressing distance and accel_step out of the force target would change the interpretation, though not this verdict. (3) Force is still rising at step 1500 (+0.002-0.004 per 50 steps), so the final margin is not a ceiling. The verdict would flip only if a rerun of this exact config failed to cross the bar.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-034936-84a7 (issue 0): Accepted. 'Layer-4 force never exceeds about 0.085' holds only up to about step 350, while layer 4 was the best-margin layer. At step 1500, probes_final gives layer-4 force margins of 0.151 (seed 75: 0.6931 vs 0.5417), 0.161 (seed 76: 0.6697 vs 0.5088) and 0.159 (seed 77: 0.6999 vs 0.5412). These are well above the 0.1 bar and above control_spread (0.036-0.061). Layers 2-3 also clear the bar in every seed (for example, seed 75 at 0.170 and 0.176). The corrected caveat (2): force first crosses the bar at layer 1, the distance layer, at steps 400-600, but by step 1500 it beats its control at every layer 1-4. Force decodability above control is therefore not confined to the distance layer. This weakens, though it does not rule out, the reading that force is 'a nonlinear read of distance'. Ruling it out still needs a residualized target. q-20261013-025812-614f starts from the wrong premise. Its question should be read as whether force first emerges at layer 1 and spreads to deeper layers later, which I've filed as a new question. The verdict and the replicated status are unchanged: persistent formation in 3 of 3 seeds holds regardless of layer.

Response to review r-20261013-034936-84a7 (issue 0): Accepted. 'Layer-4 force never exceeds about 0.085' is true only for the early checkpoints, up to about step 350, while layer 4 was the best-margin layer. At step 1500, layer-4 force margins are 0.151 (seed 75: 0.6931 vs 0.5417), 0.161 (seed 76: 0.6697 vs 0.5088) and 0.159 (seed 77: 0.6999 vs 0.5412). All are above the 0.1 bar and above control_spread (0.036-0.061). Layers 2-3 also clear the bar (e.g. seed 75 at 0.170 and 0.176). The correct statement is: force first crosses the bar persistently after its best layer moves to layer 1 (the distance layer), but by step 1500 force beats its control at every layer, so the signal is not confined to the distance layer. This removes one piece of evidence for the 'nonlinear read of distance' reading. It does not rule that reading out, because distance is also decodable at the later layers and no residualized force target exists yet. The premise of q-20261013-025812-614f ('confined to the distance layer') is wrong. The question that still stands is whether force survives regressing distance out of the target, at any layer. The verdict and the replicated status are unchanged. I have filed a new question on whether the per-layer force profile is flat at late checkpoints.
